items.why: MAJOR (b). `token-copy` has no power / toughness / colour fields, so the built-in template at parse.ts:577 deliberately drops the size and colour words of a printed "except it's a 4/4 black Zombie" (`if (/^\d+\/\d+$/.test(w) || w in COLOR_WORDS) continue;`) and keeps only extraSubtypes. Exiling a 1/1 would make a 1/1 token rather than the printed 4/4 (CR 707.2); Forge agrees with the printed text (`SetPower$ 4 | SetToughness$ 4 | SetColor$ Black | SetCreatureTypes$ Zombie`). This adds no engine op — only fields on an existing one — but it touches types.ts, schema.ts and the copy op in src/engine/, all out of scope here, so the wording stays declined. Land the fields, then the parse.ts:577 template stops discarding the words, then src/engine/ops must apply them as a copiable-values override (CR 707.2: the token is a copy of the exiled card except for the listed characteristics). Order matters: this alone does not unblock God-Pharaoh's Gift — it needs (a) as well.

items.why: Game.dealDamage is the only place that knows which permanent RECEIVED damage, and it never raises an event about it: the last line queues 'deals-damage' with ctx.obj = the SOURCE (which is why the built-in head "Whenever ~ deals damage" maps onto it and why `case 'deals-damage'` reads `fires = ctx.obj === perm`). The damaged object `o` never reaches a TriggerCtx anywhere in the engine, so no TriggerEvent a parser rule could return — core or family-declared — would ever be offered it. This one inserted line is the whole irreducible core need; everything else the family can contribute itself. NOT needed (the review is right, and the first 9.1p pass was wrong to ask for them): src/cards/types.ts (a family declares the variant by augmenting TriggerRegistry — types.ts:402 says so, and 17 such variants already exist under src/engine/ops/), src/cards/schema-core.ts (the zod half arrives via FAMILY_TRIGGER_VARIANTS, src/cards/schema.ts:28, folded in by composed()), and a `case 'dealt-damage':` arm in queueTriggers (a registry trigger is offered EVERY event above the core switch, game.ts:2263-2264, and triggerKinds() adds '*' for one so the fast-path gate lets every event through, game.ts:2210). No TriggerCtx field is added either: `by?: GameObject` already exists. With this line in place the family half is an ordinary ops wave: `declare module '../../cards/types.js' { interface TriggerRegistry { dealtDamage: DealtDamageTrigger } }` plus a matcher `(ev, perm, ctx, _s, event) => event === 'dealt-damage' && ctx.obj === perm` (with filter/controller/amount-threshold variants for the neighbourhood wordings) in a new src/engine/ops/generic-whenever-dealt.ts. Worth 43 finished cards on the paper pool (parse:why: 65 cards, 43 finishes, weight 54 — the #2 trigger-head construct).

CoreTriggerEvent's `cast` variant is a filter over the spell that was cast with no way to say "the source itself": no `self` flag, and `Filter` has `other` but never `self`. Without it there is no AST for "When you cast this spell" (CR 601.2i) at all, so the whole construct (88 paper cards / 90 lines / 44 one-line cards) is declined.

items.why: The firing seam. `Game.queueTriggers` scans `triggerPerms(s)` = `allPermanents(s)` + family `triggerSources`; a spell being cast is in the stack zone, so `queueTriggers('cast', { obj: card, player: p })` (game.ts:648, and the cascade free-cast at :1250) can never reach the cast card's own trigger. That is exactly why storm and cascade are pushed onto `pendingTriggers` by hand two lines above it. Three hunks: let the fast-path gate through for a cast with an object (`triggerKinds()` is read off the battlefield and would return early), make an `ev.self` event inert in the battlefield scan (otherwise a resolved Kozilek would fire on every later spell you cast), and add a self-cast block mirroring the `dies`/`ltb` one that already fires the leaving object's own triggers. VALIDATED in this worktree and then reverted: with the three patches applied, `tsc --noEmit` is clean and a scenario casting Kozilek, Butcher of Truth logs `Trigger: ... When you cast ~, draw four cards.` -> 4 draws -> then the spell resolves (CR 603.3b/608.2 order); without them the scenario fails `draw events 0 >= 4` and nothing at all is logged.

The reason this family looked necessary at all, and the one change that removes the whole motivation for claiming the payment sentence. `case 'unknown'` emits an `unsimulated` event; `emit` counts every non-decision event in `this.changes` (game.ts:259); `applyEffect` therefore leaves `lastHappened` true, so the `reflexive` composition.ts builds from "When you do," fires FOR FREE behind an unparsed payment (Sparktongue Dragon deals its 3 damage without the {2}{R}). An `unsimulated` event is a report, not a change. With this patch the 62 "When you do" printings are correct with the payment left `unknown`, and no parser rule has to take the player's mana to gate them.

`optional-pay` cannot carry an X cost today: `case 'optional-pay'` calls `this.findPayment(pl, e.mana)` with no x (game.ts:1194), `findPayment` declares `x = 0` (game.ts:123) and mana.ts:134 computes `generic = cost.generic + cost.x * x`, so `{X}` costs ZERO and the prompt always succeeds. Until an X payment asks the player for X, any template above must refuse `mana.x > 0` (both patched templates do), and the 13 X-cost printings of the construct stay unparsed — Wildborn Preserver, Halo Forager, Isareth the Awakener, Numa, Joraga Chieftain, Tilonalli's Summoner, Electro, Assaulting Battery, Shanna, Purifying Blade, Hollow Specter, Mortarion, Depala, Roalesk, The Disciple of Nissa. The same ask would also have to feed `x` to the `then`, whose amounts read `X` (characteristics.ts:152).

The ONLY core gap this construct has (the review is right that the other three claimed patches — src/cards/types.ts, src/cards/schema-core.ts, src/cards/render.ts — were unnecessary: a family mints its trigger event by declaration merging into TriggerRegistry, its schema through ops/<family>.schema.ts's `triggers: [...]`, and its rendering through RENDERERS['trigger:<on>']). The cycling branch of `activateAbility` (obj.def.cycling && a.abilityIndex === -2) queues no event of its own, and `discard()` raises `queueTriggers('discard', { player, obj })` with no reason field — so nothing downstream can tell a cycling-cost discard from a Mind Rot discard or a discard to hand size. Fix: thread an optional `reason` through `discard()` and set it from the cycling branch. This is CORRECTED from the first draft's patch, which raised a NEW `cycled` event BEFORE the discard so the card would still be in hand: CR 702.29c says the ability triggers "from whatever zone the card winds up in after it's cycled" (the graveyard), never the hand, and CR 702.29d says a cycling fires such a trigger only ONCE — so the reason must ride the existing `discard` event raised after `moveTo`, not a second event beside it. CR 702.29f makes typecycling a cycling, so the `cyclingSearch` path of the same branch gets the same reason. Once the reason is on the event, a parser rule family can claim the head with no further core work: `triggerKinds`'s '*' gate already lets a registry trigger hear every core event, and `triggerSources` (src/engine/ops/types.ts:172) already lets a family add non-permanent scan objects so the cycled card can hear its own trigger from the graveyard.

The major finding, confirmed. game.ts:2270 `case 'attacks'` hard-requires `ctx.player === perm.controller` and never reads `ev.controller`, so an attacks trigger about another object cannot fire when an opponent controls that object and attacks with it — you control Argentum Armor attached to your creature, an opponent takes control of the creature (Act of Treason) and attacks; the Equipment stays attached and the printed trigger fires (CR 603.2), the engine's does not. CR 702.6d governs what equip may ATTACH to, not continued attachment after a control change, so the old header's use of it to justify omitting `controller` was a misreading (that header text is gone). The `dies` branch one line above (game.ts:2268) already reads `ev.controller`, which is why the built-in "Whenever equipped creature dies" head (parse.ts:1335) emits `controller: 'any'`. The patch keeps today's behaviour for every head that omits the member. TriggerEvent's `attacks` variant needs the optional `controller` member (src/cards/types.ts) and EffectSchema/TriggerSchema the same, so this is an engine slice, not a rule-file change.
items.patch:
--- a/src/engine/game.ts
+++ b/src/engine/game.ts
@@ -2270,1 +2270,3 @@
-            case 'attacks': fires = ev.self ? ctx.obj === perm : (!ev.filter || (!!ctx.obj && matchesFilter(s, ctx.obj, ev.filter, perm))) && ctx.player === perm.controller; break;
+            // `controller` mirrors the `dies` branch above: omitted keeps the old reading (only YOUR attack fires it), 'any'
+            // is the attached-permanent case — an Equipment stays attached when an opponent gains control of its host and
+            // attacks with it, and the printed trigger still fires (CR 603.2; 702.6d is about attaching, not staying attached)

+              && (ev.controller === 'any' ? true : ev.controller === 'opponent' ? ctx.player !== perm.controller : ctx.player === perm.controller); break;
